fallacies.name: Ad Hominem
fallacies.subtitle: Character Smear & Deflection
fallacies.description: Attacking an opponent's character, personality, or background rather than engaging with the substantive empirical merits of their argument.
fallacies.psychology: Your brain is hardwired for tribal threat-detection, which naturally values assessing a speaker's social trustworthiness over parsing complex raw data. Bad actors exploit this ancient social shortcut by substituting character insults for evidence, triggering instant moral outrage. Recognizing this allows you to cleanly separate personal feelings about a messenger from the empirical validity of their claims.
fallacies.viral_example: "Don't listen to Dr. Aris's peer-reviewed climate data—he was once paid by a consulting firm so he is obviously a corrupt shill!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: If you strip away the personal insults, what actual empirical data or evidence remains in the claim?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 3: Evaluation & Ethical Assessment
fallacies.sift_strategy: Trace the primary data independent of the spokesperson's personality.

case_studies.title: The Municipal Transit Debate
case_studies.claim: "Don't listen to Councilwoman Morales's transit proposal—she got divorced last year, so how could she manage a city budget?"
case_studies.deconstruction: The attacker substitutes personal marital history for an analysis of the urban planning data and budgetary feasibility.
case_studies.correction: Evaluate the independent traffic impact studies and fiscal audits of the transit plan regardless of the sponsor's private life.

case_studies.title: The Vaccine Trial Dismissal
case_studies.claim: "Dr. Aris published peer-reviewed climate data, but he once consulted for a renewable energy firm, so his entire 10-year dataset is fraudulent!"
case_studies.deconstruction: Instead of identifying methodology errors in the peer-reviewed dataset, the critic uses perceived affiliation to dismiss empirical evidence.
case_studies.correction: Audit the raw dataset, replication studies, and peer-review findings rather than relying on character guilt by association.

case_studies.title: The Tech Whistleblower Smear
case_studies.claim: "The whistleblower who leaked internal privacy violations is just an awkward, disgruntled ex-employee looking for attention."
case_studies.deconstruction: Corporate PR attacks the whistleblower's personality and motives to distract from the leaked internal documents.
case_studies.correction: Examine the leaked internal engineering documents and verify them through independent cybersecurity audits.

case_studies.title: The Hardware Reviewer Backlash
case_studies.claim: "That journalist gave our new flagship phone a poor battery score because he is obviously a paid rival-brand fanboy."
case_studies.deconstruction: The manufacturer deflects from standardized battery benchmark tests by accusing the journalist of covert bias.
case_studies.correction: Compare the standardized battery discharge tests across multiple independent testing labs (e.g. GSMArena, AnandTech).

case_studies.title: The Security Vulnerability Report
case_studies.claim: "Senior Engineer Dave flagged a critical SQL injection flaw, but he's always so pessimistic and difficult in meetings—let's ignore it."
case_studies.deconstruction: Team leadership dismisses a severe architectural vulnerability because they dislike the engineer's communication style.
case_studies.correction: Run automated vulnerability penetration testing against the codebase to verify the severity of the flaw objectively.

fallacies.name: False Dilemma
fallacies.subtitle: Forced Black-and-White Dichotomy
fallacies.description: Artificially reducing a complex, multi-variable reality into only two extreme, mutually exclusive options while erasing all nuanced middle grounds.
fallacies.psychology: Human cognition conserves metabolic energy under stress by reducing messy, multi-variable situations into simple binary categories. Manipulators exploit this cognitive simplicity bias by manufacturing extreme either/or ultimatums that erase all viable middle ground. When you spot a forced dichotomy, you instantly regain control by asking what third and fourth options are being hidden.
fallacies.viral_example: "Either you 100% support this controversial surveillance bill, or you want terrorists to attack our schools!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: What third, fourth, or compromise alternatives are being intentionally excluded by this ultimatum?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 1: Critical Analysis of Media Content
fallacies.sift_strategy: Find Better Coverage across independent spectrums.

case_studies.title: The Surveillance Ultimatum
case_studies.claim: "Either you 100% support this omnibus surveillance bill, or you want terrorists to attack our schools!"
case_studies.deconstruction: Forces a binary choice between total privacy surrender and active support for terrorism, ignoring balanced oversight models.
case_studies.correction: Explore third options: targeted judicial warrants, encrypted data standards, and transparent civilian oversight boards.

case_studies.title: The Clean Energy False Choice
case_studies.claim: "We must either completely shut down all fossil fuel plants by next week or accept that our economy will completely collapse into poverty."
case_studies.deconstruction: Presents an abrupt shutdown versus total inaction as the only two options, erasing phased transition plans and grid modernization.
case_studies.correction: Analyze multi-year phased transition roadmaps combining renewables, battery storage, and smart grid infrastructure.

case_studies.title: The Enterprise SaaS Ultimatum
case_studies.claim: "Either upgrade to our $499/month Enterprise Ultra tier today, or accept that your data will be deleted at midnight."
case_studies.deconstruction: Manufactures a high-pressure ultimatum to force enterprise conversions when data backup and lower tiers exist.
case_studies.correction: Review export options, lower-cost archival storage, and contact customer support for standard grace periods.

case_studies.title: The Standardized Testing Debate
case_studies.claim: "Either we test students every week with standardized exams, or our children will graduate completely illiterate."
case_studies.deconstruction: Erases project-based learning, portfolio assessment, and formative classroom feedback as viable educational measurement.
case_studies.correction: Investigate hybrid assessment frameworks combining continuous portfolio evaluation with periodic diagnostic checks.

case_studies.title: The Overtime Loyalty Test
case_studies.claim: "You either work 80 hours this weekend on this launch, or you don't care about this startup's survival."
case_studies.deconstruction: Frames healthy boundaries as sabotage, ignoring efficient project scoping, workload re-allocation, and phased deliverables.
case_studies.correction: Re-prioritize milestone features, adjust release timelines, and delegate tasks without burning out the team.

fallacies.name: Appeal to Fear
fallacies.subtitle: Catastrophizing & Doomsday Bait
fallacies.description: Using terrifying, apocalyptic predictions to trigger an instinctual fight-or-flight response, forcing compliance without verification.
fallacies.psychology: Your amygdala evolved to prioritize immediate survival by triggering a rapid fight-or-flight response before your analytical prefrontal cortex can intervene. Demagogues and scammers intentionally weaponize visceral catastrophizing to induce panic and force blind compliance. Pausing to recognize the fear spike allows your rational brain to step in and demand verifiable proof before reacting.
fallacies.viral_example: "If this treaty passes tomorrow, our society will face irreversible total annihilation and economic ruin within weeks!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Does the underlying scientific consensus actually predict this catastrophic timeline, or is terror being used as persuasion?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 4: Critical Engagement & Cognitive Autonomy
fallacies.sift_strategy: Stop: Pause when feeling a surge of acute existential dread.

case_studies.title: The Invasion Border Narrative
case_studies.claim: "If this border treaty passes tomorrow, millions of violent criminals will flood your suburban neighborhood within 48 hours!"
case_studies.deconstruction: Uses visceral doomsday imagery to trigger acute fear, shutting down rational analysis of border management logistics.
case_studies.correction: Examine government census figures, crime rate statistics per capita, and bilateral enforcement provisions.

case_studies.title: The Banking System Collapse Panic
case_studies.claim: "All commercial banks will freeze withdrawals tonight at midnight! Convert your life savings into SafeGoldCoin before you lose everything!"
case_studies.deconstruction: Creates panic about immediate financial ruin to rush victims into unverified, illiquid cryptocurrency schemes.
case_studies.correction: Check official central bank announcements, FDIC insurance limits, and reputable financial regulatory wire services.

case_studies.title: The Tap Water Mind-Control Toxin
case_studies.claim: "Municipal water contains deadly nano-toxins designed to destroy your immune system! Buy our $1,200 vortex filter before it's too late!"
case_studies.deconstruction: Weaponizes fear of invisible poisoning to sell expensive, scientifically bogus water filtration hardware.
case_studies.correction: Read local municipal water quality reports (Consumer Confidence Reports) and WHO water safety thresholds.

case_studies.title: The Urgent Ransomware Alert
case_studies.claim: "URGENT: 47 trojans detected on your device! Your webcam has recorded private footage. Pay 0.5 BTC within 6 hours to prevent leak!"
case_studies.deconstruction: Classic extortion scam exploiting acute terror and shame to force immediate cryptocurrency transfers.
case_studies.correction: Never pay ransom. Disconnect network, run local offline antivirus scans, and report the phishing email to authorities.

case_studies.title: The Tablet Brain Damage Scare
case_studies.claim: "Allowing your toddler to touch a tablet for 10 minutes causes permanent, irreversible brain shrinkage and lifelong learning deficits!"
case_studies.deconstruction: Exaggerates nuanced pediatric screen time guidelines into sensationalized neurological catastrophe to generate viral ad clicks.
case_studies.correction: Consult official AAP (American Academy of Pediatrics) guidelines on co-viewing and balanced digital engagement.

fallacies.name: Confirmation Bias
fallacies.subtitle: Echo Chamber Validation
fallacies.description: The subconscious tendency to eagerly accept and share information that confirms existing prejudices while aggressively rationalizing away contrary proof.
fallacies.psychology: Your brain naturally seeks efficiency and social cohesion by favoring information that validates your existing worldview while filtering out cognitive dissonance. Algorithmic echo chambers exploit this tendency by serving emotionally gratifying narratives that make unverified claims feel intuitively true. Developing metacognitive awareness empowers you to actively seek disconfirming evidence, making your intellect far sharper and more resilient.
fallacies.viral_example: "I knew the opposing party was secretly running that ring! I won't even check if this screenshot is photoshopped because it feels so true."
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Would I scrutinize this claim more aggressively if it attacked a public figure I admire?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 5: Metacognition & Self-Reflection
fallacies.sift_strategy: Investigate the Source from counter-perspective wire services.

case_studies.title: The Viral Fake Polling Screenshot
case_studies.claim: "A blurry screenshot claims my candidate is winning by 40 points in an unreleased internal poll—I'm retweeting immediately!"
case_studies.deconstruction: The user bypasses fact-checking because the claim delivers emotional validation and aligns with their preferred outcome.
case_studies.correction: Cross-reference with five-thirty-eight or Nate Silver aggregate polling averages and verified polling methodologies.

case_studies.title: The Speculative Tech Bubble
case_studies.claim: "I only read Reddit threads praising this stock; all the mainstream financial analysts warning of bankruptcy are just corrupt short-sellers."
case_studies.deconstruction: The investor systematically filters out negative financial indicators to protect their ego and sunk investment.
case_studies.correction: Read audited 10-K filings, debt maturity schedules, and counter-thesis reports before committing capital.

case_studies.title: The Miracle Diet Testimonial
case_studies.claim: "I felt energized after drinking celery juice on Monday, so this blog claiming it cures autoimmune disease must be 100% scientific!"
case_studies.deconstruction: Attributes subjective daily variance to a single food while ignoring double-blind randomized clinical trial results.
case_studies.correction: Search PubMed or Cochrane Systematic Reviews for peer-reviewed meta-analyses on nutritional interventions.

case_studies.title: The Algorithmic Rage Loop
case_studies.claim: "Every post on my feed proves that the opposite political party is actively evil and plotting civil war."
case_studies.deconstruction: Engagement algorithms feed users content that reinforces their outrage, creating the illusion of universal consensus.
case_studies.correction: Audit recommendation algorithms by using private browsing, diverse RSS feeds, and ground-truth news aggregators.

case_studies.title: The Unconscious Interview Filter
case_studies.claim: "The candidate went to my alma mater, so their slight hesitation during the coding test was just thoughtfulness, not lack of skill."
case_studies.deconstruction: The interviewer interprets ambiguous behavior favorably for in-group candidates while penalizing out-group applicants for the same trait.
case_studies.correction: Use blinded code assessments, standardized rubric questions, and diverse multi-panel interview scorecards.

fallacies.name: Weasel Words
fallacies.subtitle: Vague & Passive Attribution
fallacies.description: Creating the illusion of widespread authoritative backing through anonymous, nebulous phrasing ('experts warn', 'many people are saying').
fallacies.psychology: Our cognitive architecture relies on linguistic authority cues to quickly absorb information without exhausting energy on deep source verification. Deceptive communicators exploit this by using passive vagueness—like 'experts say' or 'studies suggest'—to create an illusion of consensus with zero accountability. Spotting these linguistic cloaks trains you to immediately demand specific names, primary data, and methodology details.
fallacies.viral_example: "Leading scientists all agree without a doubt that this secret household spice eliminates 100% of toxins!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Which specific university, medical institution, or published paper is actually named in the body text?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 2: Verification of Information Sources
fallacies.sift_strategy: Trace Claim: Locate the original peer-reviewed publication.

case_studies.title: The Anonymous Slander Segment
case_studies.claim: "Many respected sources are now saying that the mayor might be secretly embezzling public funds."
case_studies.deconstruction: Hides behind 'many sources' to float explosive allegations without naming a single accountable investigator.
case_studies.correction: Demand named on-the-record sources, official audit documents, or formal grand jury indictments before repeating claims.

case_studies.title: The Miracle Detox Capsule
case_studies.claim: "Studies suggest that our patented formula helps support cellular rejuvenation and may fight aging."
case_studies.deconstruction: Uses vague hedging verbs ('suggests', 'supports', 'may fight') to bypass FDA drug efficacy regulations.
case_studies.correction: Check whether the product has FDA approval or peer-reviewed clinical trials demonstrating statistically significant outcomes.

case_studies.title: The Non-Apology Press Release
case_studies.claim: "Mistakes were made, and certain communications may have been misinterpreted by some stakeholders."
case_studies.deconstruction: Uses passive voice and vague quantifiers ('mistakes were made', 'some stakeholders') to avoid accepting direct responsibility.
case_studies.correction: Identify who specifically authorized the decision, what exact policies failed, and what restitution is being provided.

case_studies.title: The Phantom Majority
case_studies.claim: "It is widely believed that the public has completely lost faith in the judicial system."
case_studies.deconstruction: Substitutes 'it is widely believed' for rigorous representative polling data with published sample sizes and margins of error.
case_studies.correction: Examine Gallup, Pew Research, or academic polls with published methodologies, sample demographics, and confidence intervals.

case_studies.title: The Eco-Friendly Cleaning Spray
case_studies.claim: "Made with up to 100% naturally-derived ingredients in a virtually chemical-free process."
case_studies.deconstruction: 'Up to 100%' legally means anything from 0% to 100%, and 'naturally-derived' has zero standardized legal definition.
case_studies.correction: Look for third-party certifications like USDA Organic, EPA Safer Choice, or Cradle to Cradle standards.

fallacies.name: Artificial Urgency
fallacies.subtitle: Scam Pressure & Panic Trap
fallacies.description: Imposing artificial deadlines ('Act now in 15 minutes or your account will be deleted') to short-circuit analytical reasoning.
fallacies.psychology: The human mind operates on an evolutionary scarcity reflex, where perceived time pressure triggers an instinctual urge to act before missing out. Scammers weaponize artificial countdowns and emergency deadlines to overwhelm your working memory and short-circuit deliberate analysis. Taking a conscious 60-second breathing pause instantly breaks the psychological pressure loop and restores full analytical control.
fallacies.viral_example: "URGENT SECURITY ALERT: Your crypto wallet has been compromised. Verify your secret seed phrase within 10 minutes or lose all funds!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Why is this platform demanding instant action rather than allowing me to navigate directly through their official app?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 4: Digital Safety & Scam Resistance
fallacies.sift_strategy: Stop: Never click links inside urgent SMS, email, or DMs.

case_studies.claim: "FLASH SALE: Only 2 items left at 90% off! Your cart will expire in 04:59 minutes!"
case_studies.deconstruction: A programmed JavaScript timer resets on page refresh to induce artificial FOMO and bypass price comparison.
case_studies.correction: Use price history trackers (e.g. CamelCamelCamel, Keepa) and refresh the page to verify whether the countdown is artificial.

case_studies.title: The Immediate Arrest Warrant Call
case_studies.claim: "This is Officer Miller from the IRS. You owe $2,400 in back taxes. Pay via Target gift cards in 30 minutes or police will be at your door!"
case_studies.deconstruction: Government agencies never demand gift card payments or threaten immediate armed dispatch over a phone call.
case_studies.correction: Hang up immediately. Government revenue agencies contact taxpayers via postal mail and offer formal appeal channels.

case_studies.title: The Uninspected Apartment Deposit
case_studies.claim: "I have 15 other applicants waiting outside. Wire the $1,500 security deposit right now without a tour or I give it to someone else!"
case_studies.deconstruction: Forces the victim to wire non-refundable funds before discovering the rental listing was hijacked from another site.
case_studies.correction: Never wire money or sign leases without an in-person walkthrough and verifying property ownership through municipal land records.

case_studies.title: The Instant Remote Job Offer
case_studies.claim: "Congratulations! You are hired as a Data Analyst ($65/hr). Buy home office equipment from our vendor link within 2 hours to secure your spot!"
case_studies.deconstruction: Preys on job seekers' excitement with an urgent fake equipment portal to steal credit card details.
case_studies.correction: Legitimate corporate employers ship equipment directly or provide corporate expense accounts after formal verification.

case_studies.title: The Distressed Relative Bail Scam
case_studies.claim: "Grandma, it's me! I was in a car crash in Mexico and need $3,000 for bail right now. Don't tell Mom and Dad, please hurry!"
case_studies.deconstruction: Exploits family love and acute panic to bypass communication with other family members who would expose the lie.
case_studies.correction: Hang up and call the family member directly on their known phone number or call their parents to verify their whereabouts.

fallacies.name: Strawman Argument
fallacies.subtitle: Caricaturing & Distorting Claims
fallacies.description: Misrepresenting an opponent's nuanced argument into an absurd, extreme caricature that is ridiculously easy to knock down.
fallacies.psychology: The brain naturally prefers solving easier cognitive puzzles, making an absurdly exaggerated parody far quicker to refute than a nuanced, well-reasoned argument. Opponents exploit this mental shortcut by substituting a distorted caricature in place of what was actually said to score cheap rhetorical points. You gain the upper hand by calmly pulling the debate back to the exact original proposition and its supporting evidence.
fallacies.viral_example: "Proponents of school lunch subsidies want to replace all parental authority with totalitarian state kitchen inspectors!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Did the original advocates actually propose that extreme policy, or did the critic invent that scenario?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 1: Critical Analysis of Discourse
fallacies.sift_strategy: Trace the original quote in its complete, unedited context.

case_studies.title: The Car Ban Distortion

case_studies.deconstruction: Replaces a modest infrastructure proposal for multi-modal transit with an absurd fantasy of banning all personal vehicles.
case_studies.correction: Review the actual city council ordinance text specifying lane widths, parking offset metrics, and delivery zones.

case_studies.title: The Arts Education Debate
case_studies.claim: "Those who want to increase school art and music funding clearly hate science and want our children to fail at math and engineering."
case_studies.deconstruction: Distorts a holistic curriculum proposal into an anti-STEM crusade to make the opposing view look frivolous and dangerous.
case_studies.correction: Read the comprehensive budget breakdown showing proposed funding allocations across both STEM and humanities.

case_studies.title: The Dietary Sugar Guidelines
case_studies.claim: "Public health doctors recommending reduced added sugar intake want to outlaw birthday cakes and arrest children who eat ice cream!"
case_studies.deconstruction: Exaggerates voluntary dietary health guidelines into authoritarian food prohibitions to mock the medical consensus.
case_studies.correction: Check official Dietary Guidelines for Americans (DGA) documents to read the actual recommended daily caloric percentages.

case_studies.title: The Flexibility Distortion
case_studies.claim: "The engineering team asking for 2 days of remote work just wants to get paid for watching Netflix on the couch all day."
case_studies.deconstruction: Strawmans a structured hybrid work proposal into an accusation of complete workplace fraud and laziness.
case_studies.correction: Measure software engineering output through sprint velocity, code review throughput, and objective deliverable milestones.

case_studies.title: The Bail Reform Caricature
case_studies.claim: "Advocates for ending cash bail for non-violent offenses want to abolish all police departments and let violent bank robbers roam free."
case_studies.deconstruction: Substitutes a specific procedural reform for non-violent misdemeanors with the total abolition of criminal law enforcement.
case_studies.correction: Read the statutory text of the reform act, which explicitly maintains detention mandates for violent offenses.

fallacies.name: Bandwagon Effect
fallacies.subtitle: Social Proof Manipulation
fallacies.description: Arguing that a claim must be valid or high-quality simply because millions of people believe it or it has 10M views on TikTok.
fallacies.psychology: As social primates, humans possess deeply ingrained conformity instincts because consensus historically signaled physical safety and group belonging. Viral algorithms and marketing campaigns exploit this by fabricating the impression that 'everyone agrees,' making conformity feel like effortless wisdom. True critical thinking allows you to remember that popularity has never been a reliable metric of empirical truth.
fallacies.viral_example: "Over 5 million people bought this miracle magnetic detox bracelet this week—it can't possibly be fake!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Can millions of well-intentioned people be swayed by viral marketing or algorithmic momentum without empirical evidence?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 3: Differentiating Virality from Veracity
fallacies.sift_strategy: Investigate whether independent consumer protection agencies verified the claim.

case_studies.deconstruction: Substitutes anecdotal confirmation for large-scale epidemiological data.

case_studies.title: Bandwagon Effect in Executive Decision Making

case_studies.deconstruction: Cognitive biases cloud rational resource allocation and risk mitigation.
case_studies.correction: Establish objective, pre-defined decision scorecards and conduct blameless project post-mortems.

fallacies.name: Sunk Cost Bias
fallacies.subtitle: Entrenched Commitment Trap
fallacies.description: Refusing to abandon a discredited belief, investment, or political figure because of the enormous time, money, or reputation already invested in it.
fallacies.psychology: Your psychology possesses a natural loss-aversion bias that makes abandoning an existing investment of time, money, or belief feel like painful defeat. Deceptive systems leverage this trap to keep you doubling down on failing propositions simply because you have already committed resources. Framing your decisions around future utility rather than unrecoverable past costs gives you the mental freedom to pivot intelligently.
fallacies.viral_example: "I've already invested $5,000 into this trading scheme and defended it to all my friends. I have to put in another $2,000 to prove I was right!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: If I was discovering this situation with fresh eyes today with zero prior investment, what decision would I make?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 5: Ethical & Reflective Information Processing
fallacies.sift_strategy: Stop: Seek dispassionate third-party financial or academic counsel.

fallacies.name: Circular Reasoning
